location: Central Otago, New Zealand, near Lake Dunstan on the 45th parallel

production.waterSource: The distillery identifies Southern Alps glacial water as its whisky water source.
production.malt: 100% New Zealand barley is used for whisky. Official material identifies local distiller's malt and a separate Manuka-smoked malt made with New Zealand-grown West Coast Manuka wood.
production.stills: Scapegrace states that the Central Otago site uses Speyside-made copper stills; established specialist reporting describes a pair of copper pot stills for whisky production.
production.peat: The distillery makes both unsmoked malt whisky and Manuka-smoked malt whisky; no peat-PPM figure is published in the verified source set.
production.maturation: Official releases and cask-club disclosures include virgin French oak as a core maturation choice, alongside ex-bourbon, Pinot Noir and other cask types. The site deliberately exploits Central Otago's pronounced seasonal temperature swings during maturation.

houseCharacter: Scapegrace builds its single malt around New Zealand barley, glacial water and a modern Central Otago maturation climate with large seasonal temperature movement. Copper pot distillation provides the spirit base, while unsmoked and Manuka-smoked malt streams allow the distillery to create distinct aromatic styles without relying on Scotch-style peat conventions. French oak and local wine-cask influence then add spice, structure and regional character to the fruit-led new make.
cask23Narrative: Scapegrace is a distinctly New Zealand whisky operation rather than a copy of a Scottish template. Local barley and Southern Alps water form the base, while the distillery also uses Manuka-smoked malt to create a uniquely local smoky style. Central Otago's dramatic seasons and a cask programme that includes French oak and New Zealand wine wood make maturation as important to the identity as the spirit itself.
